approach:
Add one reading-gate check, `check_speed_timeline(reading, request)`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, wired as one `step!(check_speed_timeline(reading, request));` line in `refusing_check` right after `check_outcome_state`. Root cause, named in the doc comment, D163 and the changelog: the reading stage checked a request's own figures only if the reader chose to, so readings were planned around stated timings with no stage timeline from the code. The gate every speed request passes is where it is fixed. `speed_request(request)` decides what a speed request is, in four steps. (a) A request that has a line starting `Spec requirement: ` (hestia.rs SPEC_LINE, made `pub(crate)`) is a speed request exactly when `Priority::from_text` is High, because `spec_request` (hestia.rs:726-730) sets High only when `gap.speed` (`is_speed`) holds. Its `Requirement:` statement is never scanned, which keeps the existing choice at hestia.rs:3229-3233 that 'faster' in passing is not speed. (b) A line starting with the SLOWDOWN_MARKER or THROUGHPUT_MARKER of Hestia is a speed request. (c) `own_request_text` drops text that other people wrote. For a root-cause request it drops the `Introspection … ; prevention it proposed:` lines. For an approved-proposal request (work_decisions.rs) it drops everything from the `## Source` heading on, which copies cited records. (d) The remaining text is scanned with the whole-word and phrase cues. A speed request then needs a `Timeline:` assumption with a crates/ path, a `stages:` list of at least two stages each with a duration (unless it says no recorded timing), and a place word followed by a stage name. The fake reader gets one fixed Timeline, with a drain test pinning it.

Scope: beyond the five listed deliverables I touch four files under the request's `Files: crates/`, each with the smallest edit and each named in D163 and the changelog. They are fake.rs, hestia.rs, work_decisions.rs and drain.rs. D163 will say so.

decisions.choice: Enforce at the reading gate with one `step!` in `refusing_check` (reading.rs:3226), placed after `check_outcome_state`.
decisions.reason: Every reading passes `refusing_check`. The corpus test `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` forces a refusing case per step. No model call is needed, and a refused reading gets one re-read with the refusal text. `check_outcome_state_doc_names_root_cause_and_scope` needs `check_outcome_state` right after `check_governance_coverage`; a step after it leaves that position alone.

rejected.option: Prompt-only guidance (reader brief or reader.md)
rejected.why: It is prose only and the reader can ignore it, which is the failure. The 'mechanism' default requires a check, and reader.md is out of scope.

rejected.option: A planner-stage check (plan_findings)
rejected.why: By then the reading is accepted and the criteria are fixed around the request's figure.

rejected.option: A verifier-stage check
rejected.why: It runs after the producer built the wrong thing; the failure is in planning.

rejected.option: Have Athena run the stages at reading time
rejected.why: A build and test run per reading is unbounded cost and beyond one producer run.

decisions.choice: Quoted text written by others is never scanned. Three builders quote such text: the root-cause request (prevention lines), the spec-gap request (`Requirement:` statement) and the approved-proposal request (copied Source and Evidence). The spec request is classified by `Priority::from_text(request) == High`, which equals `is_speed` for requests built by `spec_request`. The approved-proposal request is cut at the `## Source` heading, so only its title and Proposal lines are scanned. The root-cause request drops only the Introspection prevention lines, so its Cause and Failure class lines are still scanned. Shared consts: `pub(crate) SPEC_LINE` (already a private const at hestia.rs:520), `pub const ROOT_CAUSE_MARKER`, `INTROSPECTION_PREFIX` and `PREVENTION_MARK` in hestia.rs, and `pub const APPROVED_LINE` and `SOURCE_HEADING` in work_decisions.rs. The builders format with these consts so the rendered bytes stay identical.
decisions.reason: Answers critic finding 4. I read `spec_request` (hestia.rs:691-739): the statement comes from docs/spec.toml, and the code already decided that a stray 'faster' there is not speed (`is_speed`, hestia.rs:613; test at :3056 and :3229-3233). `approve_request` (work_decisions.rs:279-313) copies the content of cited files, jobs and commits into the text, so a cue there is not this job's goal. The reason that skips prevention lines applies to all three. A person's own non-builder request is scanned whole. Priority text is a sound signal for spec requests because the only writer of a `Spec requirement:` line is `spec_request`, which sets High only for `gap.speed`; hestia.rs tests at :3087-3089 pin High versus Normal. A High spec request still needs a Timeline, as the class intends.

rejected.option: Scan the whole spec request
rejected.why: Five active statements in docs/spec.toml hold 'faster' and similar words (lines 1187, 1917, 1929, 2117, 2885 per the critic), so gap requests for them would be refused for a cue the code already rejected.

rejected.option: Scan the statement with `is_speed` also OR-ed in
rejected.why: Still scans the statement. The Priority signal alone matches `is_speed`.

rejected.option: Duplicate the marker strings in reading.rs
rejected.why: They drift from the builders. Shared consts used by both the format! calls and the detector cannot drift, and tests pass real builder output through the detector.

rejected.option: Leave approve_request text unscanned-edited (scan all of it)
rejected.why: It copies arbitrary cited records; a quoted cue would force a Timeline the job's goal does not need.

decisions.choice: Hestia's own speed requests are structural: a line starting with `hestia::SLOWDOWN_MARKER` or `hestia::THROUGHPUT_MARKER` makes `speed_request` true. Added human cues: 'takes longer' and 'takes too long' (take-form word then `longer` or `too long`), a duration after under/below/within with a wide time noun before it, a duration after `to` with a cut verb and a wide time noun before it, and a shorten verb with a narrow time noun within three words.
decisions.reason: `slowdown_request` (hestia.rs:1735) renders 'takes longer' and 'shortens that stage'. `throughput_request` (:1611) is built around 'Predicted saving: N minutes', which is the failure class: planning around a predicted timing figure. Word cues alone would see neither. The markers are already `pub const` and used by `open_request_with_marker` (:1651). Two time-noun lists: a wide one for the figure-target rules and a narrow one (time, duration, runtime, run, runs, stage, stages, wait, pipeline) for the shorten rule, so 'shorten the error message' is not a cue.

rejected.option: Leave Hestia's requests to word cues
rejected.why: 'takes longer' and 'shortens that stage' are not cues, so the slowdown request would pass unseen.

rejected.option: Treat `too long` alone as a cue
rejected.why: 'the title is too long' is not about speed.

rejected.option: One wide time-noun list for shorten
rejected.why: 'Shorten the test names' would be flagged.

decisions.choice: A cut verb (cut, cuts, save, saves, reduce, reduces, shave, shaves, trim, trims, lower, lowers) is a cue only when a duration figure is its object (the figure starts within two words after the verb, optionally after about, around, another, roughly, nearly, almost) or follows `by`/`off` within five words, with no setting word between. Setting words: timeout(s), interval(s), ttl, expiry, retention, lifetime, retry, backoff, debounce. Weak words (slow, slower, slowest, slowly, slowdown, delay, delays, delayed, timing, timings) count only after a cut verb within five words or right after `too`. Stand-alone cues: faster, quicker, speedup, latency, `speed up`, `head start`. Matching is whole-word over `request_words` (reading.rs:3503).
decisions.reason: Keeps settings changes out: 'Save the state every 30 seconds', 'Reduce the retry timeout to 10 s', 'Trim the log after 5 minutes', 'Add a retry delay setting', 'Fix a timing attack' are not cues, while 'Save 12 minutes', 'Cut 5 minutes from the checks' and 'Shave 30 s off the run' are. Rules are kept no wider than the corpus cases need (critic finding 5): each rule has an accept or refuse case, and a rule with no case is not added.

rejected.option: Any cut verb with a figure within five words
rejected.why: Flags settings changes.

rejected.option: Bare delay, timing or slow as cues
rejected.why: Common in requests that are not about speed.

rejected.option: Substring match like the fake reader's SPEED_WORDS
rejected.why: Matches inside other words and drifts from the gate.

decisions.choice: The Timeline must hold a crates/ path (`names_crates_path`, reading.rs:3838), a `stages:` clause with at least two ordered stages, a duration per stage (unless it says 'no recorded timing'), and a clause with a place word (sits, slowest, longest, bottleneck) followed by a stage name. 'No recorded timing' replaces only the durations. The gate checks the shape, not the truth of the figures; D163 and the doc comment say so.
decisions.reason: The three introspections ask for each stage in order, its measured duration and where the claimed delay sits. Stage order and place come from the code; only durations may be missing from records. A text-only gate cannot verify figures.

rejected.option: A stock 'no recorded timing' phrase plus a crates/ path clears the check
rejected.why: One fixed sentence would clear every speed request without the stage order, which is the cause.

rejected.option: Keep 'delay' as a place word
rejected.why: 'the claimed delay is real' would pass without placing the delay in a stage.

rejected.option: Check only when the request holds a duration figure
rejected.why: The class includes 'make it faster' with no figure.

decisions.choice: Keep the crates/ path requirement and state the limit in D163: a target repository with no crates/ directory cannot meet the rule.
decisions.reason: It mirrors `check_code_survey` and the reading's contract (the Timeline names the crates/ code read). Athena's own repository is the target today; a non-crates generalisation is a named follow-up.

rejected.option: Accept any slash path the reading references
rejected.why: Widens the rule beyond the reading's contract.

decisions.choice: Answers findings 1-3 (scope) and 6 (fake Timeline). Keep four files beyond the five deliverables, each with the smallest edit: fake.rs (one fixed Timeline assumption and a comment), hestia.rs (consts and tests), work_decisions.rs (two consts used by `approve_request`, with the text unchanged, and one test) and drain.rs (one new test, no existing test edited). The fake's Timeline keeps an absence phrase so it passes `check_reading_references` in a fixture repo with no crates/ (tests/common/mod.rs:144-158; ABSENCE_PHRASES reading.rs:3030).
decisions.reason: drain.rs:7008 sends 'Speed up planning' through the real gate with the fake reader, whose reading (fake.rs:283) has no Timeline, so without the fake.rs edit an existing test fails. A bare crates/ path in the fake would be refused by `check_reading_references` in every fixture-based CLI test; the fixture has no crates/ file for a Timeline path to name, so the absence phrase stays (finding 6 allowed this). athena-agent cannot call athena-core, so the pin test lives in athena-cli. The shared consts and the tests that feed real builder output to the detector belong in the files that hold the builders. All four files are under the request's `Files: crates/`.

rejected.option: Edit the drain test request to avoid the cue
rejected.why: Hides the dependency and weakens an existing test.

rejected.option: Emit the Timeline only when the fake's SPEED_WORDS match
rejected.why: SPEED_WORDS and the gate's cues differ; a nested run with a gate cue the fake misses would be refused.

rejected.option: Put the shared-const tests in reading.rs only
rejected.why: They would not call the real builders; a builder change would go unseen.

decisions.choice: Answers finding 5 (measurement). Step 9 has the producer look for stored readings and run the existing `replay` (reading.rs:4439) or `athena check-reading` (athena-cli main.rs:641) over them. D163 records the newly refused share beside the declared 5%. If no stored readings exist in the producer's snapshot, D163 says the share could not be measured, because the snapshot has no `records/` (system facts, 'Producer snapshot'), and names the replay run on the real repository as the follow-up. The 5% stays labelled an estimate.
decisions.reason: The tool exists and the plan reuses it. I cannot run it, and the producer's snapshot lacks records, so the honest record is either a measured share or a stated reason.

rejected.option: Claim a measured rate
rejected.why: Nothing here was measured.

rejected.option: Write a new measuring tool
rejected.why: The replay already counts newly refused readings.

decisions.choice: Add a seventh `READING_RULES` line of at most 218 characters naming `check_speed_timeline` and what a Timeline holds. Do not extend CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE; keep the 220-character line cap and the 2400-byte section cap.

risks.risk: False refusals: a request using a cut verb plus `by`/`off`/`to` and a figure for a non-speed purpose (for example 'Reduce the grace period by 5 minutes') is refused until the reader writes a Timeline.
risks.mitigation: Setting words, the object-of-verb rule and the time-noun requirement for the `to`/`under` forms keep the common settings forms out, pinned by accept cases. The reader gets one re-read with refusal text saying what to write, and can use the no-recorded-timing form. The 5% is an estimate, measured only if stored readings are available (step 9).

risks.risk: Builders that quote other text and are not skipped (accept_request, blind_spot_request, the design review's failed-job titles) could carry a stray cue and force a Timeline.
risks.mitigation: Cues are phrase-based, not bare words. The fixed text of those builders holds none (read). The reader gets one re-read. D163 states the limit and the follow-up of skipping those quoted parts if the replay shows they matter.

risks.risk: Spec requests are classified by the Priority line, so a hand-written request with a `Spec requirement:` line and `Priority: high` is treated as a speed request.
risks.mitigation: Only `spec_request` writes that line (hestia.rs:710), and the worst effect is a Timeline asked for; a hestia.rs test pins High versus Normal against `is_speed`.

risks.risk: Scanning the Cause line means a root-cause request whose cause text holds a stray cue needs a Timeline.
risks.mitigation: Phrase-based rules. A hestia.rs test pins this job's own visible Cause as not a speed request. A cause that is truly about slowness is meant to need one.

risks.risk: Hestia's throughput design request, which only edits docs/design/, now needs a Timeline.
risks.mitigation: It names a Stage and predicted minutes, the class this change targets. The no-recorded-timing form covers missing run data. Pinned by an accept twin.

risks.risk: The check judges the shape of the Timeline, not whether the figures are measured, so a reader can write invented numbers.
risks.mitigation: Stated as a limit in the doc comment and D163. The check still forces the crates/ path, the ordered stages and the stage where the delay sits into the reading before the criteria are fixed. Checking figures against run data is a named follow-up.

risks.risk: A target repository with no crates/ directory cannot meet the crates/ path rule.
risks.mitigation: Stated as a limit in D163; Athena's own repository is the target today; the rule mirrors `check_code_survey`.

risks.risk: The reading-rules section may pass the 2400-byte or 220-character cap (briefs.rs:4430); the size figure is a hand count.
risks.mitigation: Keep the new rule at 218 characters or fewer; `cargo test -p athena-context briefs` asserts both caps. Never raise a cap.

risks.risk: The prevention-line skip or the `## Source` cut misses a builder line shape, so a quoted cue triggers a false speed request.
risks.mitigation: `one_line` flattens the prevention (hestia.rs:482-485). Tests feed real builder output through the detector, and shared consts mean a builder change that breaks a skip fails those tests.

risks.risk: Hand-written corpus fixtures trip an earlier check and refuse for the wrong reason.
risks.mitigation: Build each case from `base_reading` and change one field; name only crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs in Timeline text; copy the retry case's summary, deliverable and out_of_scope from `retry-complaint-reading-names-the-job` (refusal_corpus.rs:630-647). The corpus asserts the refusing check's name.

risks.risk: Stored Proposed readings of speed requests are dropped from the steward queue (steward.rs:421) after the change.
risks.mitigation: This is the effect of every new reading check; the declared share covers it and the steward leaves them for a person. Named in D163 and the changelog.

risks.risk: The rule count edit (6 to 7) and the INPUT_FORMS length edit could read as weakening existing tests.
risks.mitigation: They are forced by an added rule and added tags; all line, size and name-check assertions stay and gain the new check name. The summary says so.

risks.risk: Four files beyond the listed deliverables (fake.rs, hestia.rs, work_decisions.rs, drain.rs) widen scope.
risks.mitigation: All are under the request's `Files: crates/`; each edit is minimal and necessary; the changelog and D163 name them.

risks.risk: The replay of stored readings may be impossible in the producer's snapshot, because `records/` is absent.

demonstrations.method: Run the refusal corpus. A new `speed_timeline_cases()` in refusal_corpus.rs is added to `cases()`. Each Refuse case is `Expected::Refuse("check_speed_timeline")` and is built from `base_reading()` with one field changed, so no earlier check refuses it. Input forms and case ids: plain request 'Move the call earlier to save 12 minutes.' = `speed-request-without-a-timeline`; dash bullet = `speed-word-in-a-dash-bullet`; star bullet = `speed-word-in-a-star-bullet`; `1.` part = `speed-word-in-a-numbered-dot-part`; `2)` part = `speed-word-in-a-numbered-paren-part`; `(a)` part = `speed-word-in-a-lettered-paren-part`; retry complaint = `retry-complaint-still-too-slow-without-a-timeline`; a request that cites a job without relying on it = the existing root-cause cases at refusal_corpus.rs:604-617 stay Accept, plus new `root-cause-request-with-its-own-speed-goal-without-a-timeline` (Refuse); a crate-relative path = `timeline-with-a-crate-relative-path` (Refuse, names src/reading.rs); a brand word or environment variable is not read by this rule, so no case is added (the rule reads only whole words and durations). More Refuse cases: `root-cause-request-whose-cause-is-slowness-without-a-timeline`, `slowdown-request-without-a-timeline`, `throughput-design-request-without-a-timeline`, `high-priority-spec-request-without-a-timeline`, `approved-proposal-title-with-a-cue-without-a-timeline`, `takes-too-long-without-a-timeline`, `get-the-checks-under-6-minutes-without-a-timeline`, `reduce-ci-time-to-6-minutes-without-a-timeline`, `shorten-the-run-without-a-timeline`. Timeline-defect Refuse cases: `timeline-without-a-crates-path`, `timeline-with-one-stage-only`, `timeline-stage-without-a-duration`, `timeline-says-no-recorded-timing-without-stages`, `timeline-without-where-the-delay-sits`, `timeline-place-word-names-no-stage`, `timeline-label-not-at-the-start`.
